description: Business definitions and query rules for the online shop database.

terms.definition: The total amount spent by a customer across all their orders.
The number of orders placed by a customer.
The revenue generated by a product through sold order items.
The total number of units sold for a product.
A customer who has placed at least one order.
terms.condition: EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders WHERE orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id)

terms.definition: A product that has no associated order items.
terms.condition: NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items WHERE order_items.product_id = products.product_id)

business_rules: Customer spend must be calculated using orders.total, not by summing product prices.
Order count must count orders, not order items.
Product quantity sold must be calculated using order_items.quantity.
Product revenue must be calculated by multiplying order_items.quantity by products.price.
For revenue calculations based on actual sales, use INNER JOIN so that only products with sales contribute to the result.
Use LEFT JOIN when the question explicitly requires retaining all entities, including those without related records.
When the question asks for every product, include products with no sales.
Do not use LEFT JOIN automatically for every product or revenue aggregation.
Use COALESCE(SUM(...), 0) when the question requires missing aggregates to be displayed as zero.
Use HAVING to filter groups based on aggregate values.
Use WHERE to filter individual rows before aggregation.
